claims.text: Michigan governor Stevens T. Mason was 24 years old

claims.text: Maumee Harbor was seen as very valuable

claims.text: Congress rejected Michigan's 1833 convention request over the Toledo Strip
claims.quote: Congress rejected the request because of the still-disputed Toledo Strip

claims.text: Michigan's law threatened a fine up to 1000 dollars
claims.quote: under penalty of a fine up to $1,000

claims.text: And up to five years of hard labor
claims.quote: up to five years imprisonment at hard labor

claims.quote: along with General John Bell and about 600 other fully armed militiamen

claims.text: Mason occupied Toledo with around 1000 armed men

claims.text: Michigan press welcomed Ohio to hospitable graves

claims.text: At Phillips Corners Michigan says it fired only into the air

claims.text: Nine Ohio men were taken prisoner
claims.quote: nine of our men, who did not leave the ground in time

claims.text: The only battle had no casualties

claims.text: The only blood was a non-fatal stabbing of an officer
claims.quote: The only blood spilled was the non-fatal stabbing of a law enforcement officer.

claims.quote: Two Stickney stabbed Wood with a penknife and fled into Ohio

claims.text: Ohio was a crucial swing state

claims.text: Michigan had only a single non-voting delegate
claims.quote: had only a single non-voting delegate

claims.text: Jackson removed Mason as governor
claims.quote: Jackson removed Mason as Michigan's territorial governor

claims.text: Ohio judges held a midnight court
claims.quote: the judges held a midnight court before quickly retreating

claims.text: Michigan offered western three-quarters of the Upper Peninsula
claims.quote: Michigan would be granted the western three-quarters of what is now known as the Upper Peninsula

claims.text: September 1836 convention rejected the offer
claims.quote: a September 1836 special convention in Ann Arbor rejected the offer

claims.text: Michigan was nearly bankrupt from militia costs
claims.quote: nearly bankrupt because of the high militia expenses

claims.text: Federal surplus of 400000 dollars would go only to states
claims.quote: a $400,000 surplus

claims.text: Surplus to be distributed to states, not territories

claims.text: Second convention accepted terms December 14, 1836
claims.quote: The war unofficially ended on December 14, 1836

claims.text: It was called the Frostbitten Convention
claims.quote: the event became known as the Frostbitten Convention

claims.text: Michigan became a state January 26, 1837
claims.quote: On January 26, 1837, Michigan was admitted to the Union as the 26th state

claims.text: Upper Peninsula considered worthless wilderness
claims.quote: The Upper Peninsula was considered a worthless wilderness by almost all familiar with the area

claims.text: Copper and iron discovered in the 1840s

claims.text: Mining boom lasted into the 20th century
claims.quote: led to a mining boom that lasted long into the 20th century
